answer: Copying the same citations across 222 aliases as a result burns the authoring cost 222 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the horizon index resolves every citation against the trellis checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the pigment audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 4708 identities would post 554 proofs and burn roughly 38 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
